title: Small individual-investor landlords: large segment, no customer problem yet evidenced

history.reason: Segment-size signal from HUD/Census; no pain point established.

description: Nearly half of US rental units are in 1-4 unit properties, and 70 percent of those small properties are owned by individual investors; whether these owners have a specific unmet administrative problem is not yet evidenced.
customer_segment: Individual-investor owners of 1-4 unit rental properties.
context: Scoping record only: this establishes segment size, not a problem. Do not treat as validated demand.

evidence.text: About 46 percent of 49.5 million rental units are in 1-4 unit properties, and 70 percent of those properties are owned by individual investors.

alternatives: Property-management software and services: not investigated.

contradictory_evidence.text: Segment size alone does not show an unmet problem or willingness to pay.

uncertainty: Unknown: management practices, rent collection and screening pain, tool adoption, and spend. This record exists to avoid re-scoping the segment.
open_questions: How do small landlords currently collect rent, screen tenants and keep records?
Which tasks cause the most time or loss?
next_actions: Read Census RHFS tables on management and operating expenses, then seek primary evidence of specific pain points.
